title: Build Your Layoff Plan Before You Need It
meta_description: Prepare for reduced hours or job loss with a current résumé, essential budget, cash runway, benefits map and verified transition checklist.

sections.heading: Prepare for an Income Gap Without Predicting a Recession
paragraphs: A recession checklist is useful because income can change without warning, not because every market slowdown produces a layoff. Industry conditions, employer finances, role concentration and household obligations matter more than a dramatic headline.

Preparation while employed has three advantages: wages can fund reserves, benefits information is accessible and career conversations are less urgent. The objective is optionality, not panic, secrecy or disengagement from current work.

The opening photograph shows a résumé beside a laptop so the first message is unmistakable: career continuity is an asset that needs maintenance before an application deadline. Update evidence of work while projects, dates and results are easy to verify.

Do not assume an employer rumor is fact. Use official communications, required notices and direct questions where appropriate. Avoid forwarding confidential material or taking company property under the label of personal preparation.

Define the household’s exposure. One income supporting several people, a specialized role, employer-linked health coverage, variable hours or high fixed costs can require more runway than a dual-income household with flexible expenses.

Write three scenarios: hours reduced, one income lost and all household earned income interrupted. For each, identify the first bill date, available cash, insurance deadline and fastest lawful income option.

Keep normal retirement and debt decisions in context. Hoarding every dollar can sacrifice valuable matching or create expensive interest; aggressive payoff can leave no cash for rent after a layoff. Balance depends on current risk and liquidity.

Choose triggers before anxiety rises. A formal notice, eliminated project, reduced hours or confirmed closure can activate the transition budget. A weak news day should not automatically cancel investing, insurance or necessary spending.
Include nonfinancial readiness: sleep, health care, childcare backup, transport and trusted contacts. A job search requires functioning time and attention, not only cash.
The plan works when it supports the current job and can be activated quickly without pretending a downturn date or layoff probability is known.

sections.heading: Build a Private Employment File and Current Résumé
paragraphs: Create a personal employment file using lawful, nonconfidential records: offer letter, job description, pay statements, benefit summaries, performance reviews, certifications and contact details for human resources and plan administrators.

Do not copy customer lists, proprietary code, internal forecasts, trade secrets or restricted work samples. Ask permission before retaining a portfolio item. Career readiness does not override confidentiality, privacy or intellectual-property duties.

Update the résumé with outcomes rather than generic tasks. Record scope, measurable result, tools and collaborators. Replace confidential figures with approved ranges or public outcomes when necessary.

Create a master résumé and shorter versions for likely roles. Keep plain-text content for application systems and a readable formatted version for people. Confirm dates, titles and credentials; inconsistencies can delay hiring.

Write five concise accomplishment stories using situation, action and result. Include a difficult problem, collaboration, conflict, failure or correction, and a result relevant to the next role. Interview preparation is easier while memories are current.

List references and ask permission before sharing their details. Use personal contact information rather than a work email that may disappear. Note each reference’s relationship and the projects they can discuss.

Export personal performance records only through allowed channels. Separate personal contacts from employer systems without mass-downloading directories. Respect coworkers who do not want private information retained.

Review public professional profiles for accuracy and consistency. Remove sensitive details such as personal documents, full address and identifying numbers. Turn on multifactor authentication because a compromised profile can disrupt a job search.
Build a work-sample inventory: public links, approved presentations, published writing, certifications and descriptions of confidential work that demonstrate skill without exposing content.

[[S1|CareerOneStop’s job-search guides]] recommend targeting the résumé, researching employers, requesting references and preparing for interviews. The file is ready when an application can be tailored without accessing the former employer.

sections.heading: Calculate the Household’s Essential Monthly Burn
paragraphs: Runway begins with the amount required to keep the household safe and employable. List housing, utilities, food, transport, insurance, medication, childcare, minimum debt payments, taxes and essential connectivity.

Separate essential, reducible and pausable costs. A gym might pause immediately; childcare may fall only after work ends but return for interviews; professional software might be needed more during a search. Timing matters.

Use statement averages and actual renewal dates. Monthly estimates can miss quarterly insurance, annual registration, school costs and tax payments. Convert each to a monthly equivalent and note when cash is due.

Create a transition budget distinct from the current lifestyle budget. It should preserve housing, health, food, transport and job-search capacity without assuming every discretionary expense vanishes overnight.

Model reduced hours before total job loss. An income cut may preserve benefits but create a recurring deficit. Calculate the gap and identify which transfers, subscriptions or extra debt payments pause first.

Include job-search costs: interview clothing, transportation, childcare, credential renewal, printing, connectivity and potential travel. Verify whether an American Job Center or other program can assist before paying a high-fee service.

Do not count a credit-card limit as runway. Borrowing capacity can be reduced, and interest turns an income gap into a longer recovery. Count settled cash and confirmed income separately from available credit.
If relatives may help, discuss amount, timing and whether support is a gift or loan before an emergency. Do not put uncertain family assistance in the base plan.

Mark priority consequences. Missing rent, mortgage, insurance, taxes or secured debt can be more damaging than delaying an unsecured extra payment. Seek qualified guidance when the budget cannot cover priorities.
The essential burn is credible when it can be traced to bills, reflects a lean but livable month and includes the costs required to return to work.

sections.heading: Map Every Benefit Before Access Changes
paragraphs: Employment connects more than wages. Inventory health, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, retirement plans, stock compensation, flexible accounts, commuter benefits, paid leave, education support and employee assistance programs.

Download current summary plan descriptions and administrator contacts through approved employee systems. Record coverage dates, payroll deductions, deductibles, vesting and claim procedures without storing sensitive files on an insecure device.

Confirm what happens to unused paid time off under employer policy and state law. Do not assume it will be paid. Record the balance and applicable policy, but treat payment as unconfirmed until documented.

For health coverage, identify the final active date and alternatives: a spouse’s plan, Marketplace coverage, Medicaid or CHIP where eligible, and COBRA or state continuation. Compare premium, network, deductible and effective date.

Flexible spending accounts can have deadlines and employment-related rules. Health savings accounts are generally individually owned, while FSAs differ. Check the plan rather than applying one account’s rules to another.
Review disability claims before employment ends if illness or injury affects work. Deadlines, definitions and coverage status matter. Seek plan or legal help for complex circumstances.
Employer life insurance may end or offer conversion or portability. Compare cost and need before acting. Do not assume an employer amount remains after separation.

Stock options, restricted stock and employee purchase plans can have separation deadlines and tax consequences. Obtain plan documents and qualified advice; an exercise window is not an instruction to invest.
Record retirement account plan name, administrator, balance, beneficiary and vesting. Your own contributions are yours, while employer money may depend on plan vesting rules.
The benefit map is complete when the household knows which protections stop, continue, convert or require a decision—and the date each decision becomes urgent.

sections.heading: Reduce Fragility Without Cutting the Tools of Employment
paragraphs: Lower fixed costs before income falls, but protect health, transport, childcare, connectivity and credentials needed to work. A cheaper budget that blocks the next job is false economy.

Review subscriptions, mobile plans, broadband, insurance renewals, storage and memberships by annual value. Cancel unused services only after checking contract terms, shared use and data export needs.
Avoid taking on new financed purchases from uncertain overtime, bonus or promotion income. Test the payment against the transition budget, including insurance, maintenance and fees.
If high-rate debt is present, keep minimums current and choose extra payments alongside the reserve target. Paying a balance to zero while leaving no cash can force the next bill back onto the card.

Call lenders before a missed payment when hardship appears likely. Ask about options, credit reporting, interest, fees and documentation. A temporary lower payment can extend cost, so understand the full terms.
Check insurance deductibles. Raising an excess may reduce premium but increases the cash needed after a loss. The emergency plan should be able to absorb the chosen deductible.

Preserve professional memberships only when they support credentials, leads or required continuing education. Ask about unemployed-member rates or hardship options rather than canceling automatically.
Review tax withholding after a spouse’s job change, reduced hours or other material event using official tools. A larger net check is not a saving if it creates an avoidable tax balance.

Set a pause order for automated transfers: discretionary goal, extra debt, taxable investing and then other optional flows. Essential bills, insurance and minimums remain protected unless a formal alternative is arranged.
Fragility falls when the household needs less cash each month without sacrificing the systems that preserve income, health and reemployment.

sections.heading: Create Work Leads Before Asking for Rescue
paragraphs: Networking while employed should be normal professional participation, not a sudden broadcast of fear. Reconnect with former coworkers, clients where permitted, professional groups, alumni and people in adjacent roles.

Offer useful contact before requesting help: share public information, congratulate work, answer a question or make an appropriate introduction. Relationships built only during crisis are weaker and more stressful.

Create a target list of roles, employers and adjacent industries. Note required skills, compensation range, location, work arrangement and likely hiring cycle. This turns generic networking into specific learning.
Schedule two low-pressure conversations each month. Ask how the field is changing, which skills matter and what hiring managers misunderstand. Do not ask a contact to guarantee a job.

Identify transferable evidence. A project manager may demonstrate prioritization across industries; a salesperson may show pipeline analysis; an operator may show quality and process control. Translate work into outcomes the next employer recognizes.

Close one high-value skill gap while employed. Choose a credential or work sample visible in current job postings, not an expensive program marketed through fear. Verify employer tuition assistance and repayment terms.
Maintain a personal contact method and calendar reminders. Do not conduct an external search on company devices or during restricted work time if policy prohibits it.
Prepare a truthful explanation for transition that does not disparage the employer or disclose confidential events. A layoff is a business event, not evidence of personal failure.
Build a short list of recruiters with relevant placements and verify identities. Legitimate recruiters generally do not require candidates to buy equipment through a check or pay for access to a job.
The network is ready when several people understand the work you do, the problems you can solve and the kinds of roles worth mentioning.

sections.heading: Build Cash Runway in Stages
paragraphs: The midpoint photograph shows cash entering a savings jar because a layoff reserve has one clear purpose: buying time for bills and a careful search. The account should be liquid, low-fee and appropriately insured.

Start with the next likely disruption, then one month of essential burn, then additional months based on household risk. There is no honest universal target; job stability, dependents, health, severance expectations and alternative income all matter.

[[S2|CFPB worker guidance]] explains that emergency savings can help cover bills after lost work without skipping other obligations or borrowing. Automatic transfers from each paycheck can build the reserve while income continues.

Keep predictable annual costs in separate sinking funds so they do not consume layoff runway. Car registration and insurance renewal are not job-loss emergencies simply because they arrive during unemployment.

Use settled balances only. Do not count a pending bonus, expected tax refund, unvested stock or possible severance. Create a second line for contingent resources so the base plan remains conservative.
If the household has two incomes, decide whether the reserve protects one-income loss or both. Model the surviving income after payroll deductions and new costs such as health coverage.
Balance cash with high-rate debt. A starter reserve prevents immediate reborrowing; after that, compare guaranteed interest cost with the value of extra liquidity under current layoff risk.
Choose access deliberately. A separate savings account can reduce casual spending, but emergency money should not be locked where penalties, market loss or transfer delays prevent timely bills.
Automate a dollar or percentage and increase it after a raise or debt payoff. If transfers are repeatedly reversed, lower them and repair the budget instead of recording fictional savings.
The runway is usable when its balance, monthly burn and estimated months are updated, and the household knows exactly which event authorizes withdrawals.

sections.heading: Read Warning Signs Without Sabotaging the Current Job
paragraphs: Preparation should improve present performance. Continue meeting responsibilities, documenting decisions and communicating professionally. Withdrawing effort because layoffs seem possible can damage references and remove options.

Distinguish business signals from ordinary workplace noise. Sustained revenue pressure, canceled projects, hiring freezes, facility notices and repeated hour reductions can justify a higher readiness level, but none proves an individual outcome.

Use public company information and official employee communication. Do not trade securities on material nonpublic information, spread confidential forecasts or solicit restricted details from coworkers.

The federal WARN Act and state laws can require advance notice for certain covered plant closings and mass layoffs, but coverage, exceptions and thresholds are specific. Lack of notice does not guarantee safety, and a rumor does not establish eligibility.
Ask practical questions without demanding certainty: whether priorities changed, which work is essential and what skills the team needs. The answers can improve performance even if no layoff occurs.
Avoid mass-applying from a work device, printing résumés at the office or taking recruiter calls during duties against policy. Use personal equipment, personal time and lawful channels.
If hours fall, update the reduced-income budget immediately and preserve records. Check whether partial unemployment or other assistance may apply through the official state agency; rules vary.

When a warning trigger is confirmed, increase cash temporarily by pausing the preselected optional flows. Do not cancel essential insurance or abandon all retirement saving automatically; use the written priority order.
Protect relationships. Managers and coworkers may also lack information. Accusations and public speculation can outlast the event and weaken the network needed later.

Review the trigger level weekly rather than reacting to every meeting. If conditions stabilize, restore paused transfers deliberately. If evidence worsens, complete pending medical, benefit and career tasks without manufacturing urgency for the household.
The warning-sign protocol is successful when facts change readiness actions proportionally while current work, ethics and confidentiality remain intact.

sections.heading: Write the First 72 Hours After a Layoff
paragraphs: A transition checklist reduces decisions during shock. First obtain the written notice, effective date, final-pay information, benefit dates, severance documents and property-return instructions. Do not sign immediately when review time is available.
Preserve lawful personal records and return employer equipment, badges and data as directed. Do not wipe devices, forward restricted files or retain customer information.

Apply for unemployment insurance promptly through the state’s official system if potentially eligible. [[S3|CareerOneStop notes]] that applicants generally need employer details, work dates and the reason employment ended; state rules and appeals govern eligibility.
Do not assume severance makes a claim unnecessary. Report it accurately and let the state determine its effect. Continue required weekly certifications while a claim is reviewed.
Activate the transition budget and pause transfers in the prewritten order. Preserve essential payments and contact providers before due dates when the runway is insufficient.
Notify the household with facts: final work date, confirmed cash, benefit deadlines and next review. Avoid promising a new job date. Agree on which spending changes begin immediately.
Book medical appointments or refill prescriptions appropriately before coverage ends, but do not stockpile or seek unnecessary care. Confirm coverage and provider instructions.
Update résumé dates and professional profiles after the separation is official. Contact references and priority network leads with a concise explanation and target role.
Create a claim folder for notices, pay statements, benefit elections, applications and communication logs. Track confirmation numbers and deadlines.
The first 72 hours succeed when legal and benefit deadlines are protected, cash controls activate and the search begins without destroying evidence or professional relationships.

sections.heading: Price Health Coverage Before the Deadline
paragraphs: Job loss can change health coverage quickly, and the cheapest premium is not automatically the lowest total risk. Compare effective date, network, prescriptions, deductible, out-of-pocket maximum and household eligibility.

[[S4|HealthCare.gov explains]] that losing job-based coverage can create a Marketplace Special Enrollment Period. Applications may be made within the applicable window, and documentation of lost coverage may be required.

COBRA can continue the same group coverage temporarily for eligible people, but former employees commonly pay the full premium plus any allowed administrative charge. The plan notice and federal or state rules control.
Compare a spouse’s employer plan and its special-enrollment deadline. Ask the plan administrator which documents and dates apply; do not wait for the next open enrollment without checking.
Medicaid and CHIP eligibility depends on state, income and household factors. A Marketplace application can screen for programs, but official determinations govern.
Coordinate care in progress. Provider network, prior authorization, prescription formulary and deductible progress can make continuation valuable even at a higher premium.
Know when coverage ends. Final employment date and final health-coverage date may differ. Avoid a gap created by assuming coverage lasts through month-end.
Keep COBRA election, premium and notice deadlines visible even while comparing alternatives. Voluntarily dropping COBRA later does not always create a new Marketplace enrollment opportunity.
Use official sites and plan contacts. Health-insurance scams can intensify after layoffs; verify agents, plan type and coverage before paying.
The decision is complete when every household member has a documented coverage path and the premium is included in the transition budget.

sections.heading: Handle Severance, Retirement and Taxes Separately
paragraphs: Severance is a contract or policy question, not guaranteed income. Review amount, payment timing, benefits, release language, confidentiality, non-disparagement, restrictive covenants and applicable review or revocation periods.
Consider qualified legal advice when rights, discrimination, commissions, equity or restrictive terms are material. Do not rely on a coworker’s package; agreements can differ.
Treat a lump sum as runway, not a windfall. Estimate withholding and net receipt, reserve essential months and avoid raising recurring spending. Actual tax depends on the year’s full facts.
Confirm final wages, commissions, expense reimbursements and paid-time-off treatment under policy and state law. Keep calculations and report discrepancies promptly.

For a 401(k), compare leaving assets in the plan, rolling to a new employer plan where accepted, rolling to an IRA, or taking a distribution. Fees, investments, creditor rules, loans and tax consequences differ.
Do not rush a retirement rollover because of an unsolicited call. Contact the plan administrator through known information and use a direct trustee-to-trustee process where appropriate.
An outstanding plan loan can create deadlines and tax consequences after separation. Read the plan and seek tax advice before assuming repayment or offset treatment.
Review vesting and beneficiary records. Employee contributions are vested; employer contributions may depend on the plan schedule. Confirm the separation date used by the administrator.
If stock compensation is involved, record expiration, vesting and tax dates. Do not exercise solely because a window is closing without understanding concentration and cash needs.
These decisions are complete only when each pool—cash compensation, health benefits and retirement assets—has its own documented treatment rather than one hurried “roll everything” action.

sections.heading: Protect the Search From Scams and Account Loss
paragraphs: Job seekers are attractive targets because urgency and personal data are both present. Be suspicious of text-only interviews, immediate offers, unusually high pay, requests for gift cards, cryptocurrency or money movement.

A fake-check employer may send funds for equipment and demand repayment or a purchase from a named vendor. Banks can make funds appear available before discovering the check is fraudulent. Never send money onward from an employer check.

[[S5|The FTC warns]] that honest employers do not charge candidates to obtain a job. Verify the company through a known website and contact, not the link or phone number supplied in an unexpected message.

Use a dedicated job-search email, unique password and multifactor authentication. Limit the résumé’s address and personal details. Do not include Social Security number, banking information or identity documents on a public résumé.
Provide tax and direct-deposit information only after verifying a real employer and secure onboarding process. A professional-looking portal can still be a credential theft site.

Check recruiter email domains carefully and call the company’s published number. Search for the role on the official careers page, while recognizing that legitimate recruiters may work through contracted firms.
Protect unemployment accounts with strong credentials and alerts where available. Report suspected identity theft to the state agency and official identity-theft resources promptly.
Keep current devices patched and avoid conducting sensitive applications over untrusted public networks. Back up the résumé and records securely.
Do not post severance documents, claim notices or benefit screenshots publicly when asking for advice. Redact identifiers and confidential terms.
The secure search shares only the information required at each verified stage and never pays for the promise of employment.

sections.heading: Run a Thirty-Day Transition Rehearsal
paragraphs: Practice one month on the transition budget while still employed and transfer the difference to the reserve. This tests whether the plan is livable and exposes missing categories without pretending income has already stopped.

During week one, verify employment records, benefits contacts, résumé and references. During week two, calculate burn and health premiums. During week three, contact two network leads. During week four, reconcile the rehearsal.
Do not cancel useful services merely for the test. Place their cost in the transition category and model the cancellation date. The rehearsal should avoid penalties or loss of work tools.
Track time as well as money. Estimate hours for applications, networking, interviews, training, childcare and rest. A plan requiring ten focused hours every day may fail quickly.
Simulate one reduced-income paycheck and test autopay timing. Confirm which transfers pause, which bills remain and how the checking cushion responds.
Ask a partner or trusted person to review deadlines and account access. The reviewer may find an insurance assumption, shared subscription or missing password-recovery method.
Choose weekly search metrics under personal control: tailored applications, conversations, work samples and follow-ups. An offer date is not controllable and should not be the only measure.
Protect physical and mental health. A sustainable schedule includes sleep, movement, care and social contact. Use employee assistance or community resources before access changes where appropriate.
At day thirty, update the essential burn, reserve months, résumé gaps and benefit decision sheet. Keep what worked and remove unnecessary complexity.
The rehearsal is successful when the household can explain the first month, identify weak points and return to normal spending without treating preparation as permanent deprivation.

sections.heading: Turn Interview Readiness Into a Live Opportunity
paragraphs: The late photograph shows a résumé visible during an office handshake so the placement clearly marks the final transition: preparation becoming a real employment conversation. A strong plan aims to preserve choice long enough to evaluate the next role.

Build interview examples for technical skill, judgment, collaboration, conflict and measurable results. Practice concise answers aloud and prepare questions about role scope, team stability, performance expectations and benefits.

Research the employer’s official filings, site, products and recent credible reporting. Do not interrogate an interviewer about rumors; ask how the role is funded, why it is open and what success looks like.
Prepare a compensation floor from the transition budget and market evidence, but evaluate total compensation: health premiums, retirement match, leave, commute, schedule, equipment and job stability.
Never conceal material facts or invent employment. Explain a layoff factually: role eliminated, organization changed or business closed, followed by the work and target now.

Keep multiple leads active until a written offer is verified and contingencies are complete. Verbal enthusiasm is not income. Do not stop unemployment certifications prematurely without checking state requirements.
Review the offer, start date, background-check process and benefit waiting period. A later start can require additional runway and temporary health coverage.
Negotiate professionally where appropriate, using role scope and market evidence rather than the household’s financial pressure. Request the final terms in writing.
Once employed, rebuild the reserve, revisit withholding and benefits, and preserve the career file. A new job ends one transition but not the value of readiness.
The recession checklist is finished when the worker can move from present employment to a verified next opportunity without improvising every financial, benefit and career decision under pressure.

summary: Prepare for an income interruption without pretending to predict a recession or layoff date. Define household exposure, write reduced-hours and job-loss scenarios, and select factual triggers that activate the transition budget.

Build a lawful personal employment file with offer documents, pay statements, benefit summaries, performance records, certifications and administrator contacts. Never retain confidential employer, customer or proprietary material.

Keep a current master résumé, tailored role versions, accomplishment stories, approved work samples and reference permissions. Use personal contact details that will remain available after employer access ends.

Calculate essential monthly burn from housing, utilities, food, transport, insurance, medicine, childcare, minimum debt payments and connectivity. Include annual bills and job-search costs rather than counting only monthly subscriptions.

Inventory health, disability, life, retirement, paid leave, flexible accounts, stock compensation and education benefits. Record final coverage dates, vesting, administrator contacts and every deadline.

Reduce fixed costs without cutting health, transport, childcare, connectivity or credentials needed to stay employed. Balance extra debt payoff with enough liquid cash to avoid borrowing immediately after a disruption.

Build runway in stages using a liquid, low-fee and appropriately insured account. Count settled cash, not possible severance, bonuses, refunds or unvested equity. Keep predictable annual costs in separate sinking funds.

Maintain professional relationships before a crisis. Identify target roles and industries, translate transferable outcomes, close one verified skill gap and hold low-pressure conversations with relevant contacts.

Write the first 72-hour checklist now: obtain the written notice and benefit dates, preserve lawful records, return employer property, apply promptly through the official state unemployment system and activate the transition budget.

Compare COBRA, Marketplace coverage, a spouse’s plan and public-program eligibility using actual premium, network, deductible, prescription and effective-date information. Protect all enrollment and election deadlines.
Treat severance, final wages, retirement accounts and stock compensation separately. Review release terms, tax effects, vesting, plan loans and rollover options before signing or transferring assets.

Protect the search from fake checks, paid job promises, text-only interviews and identity theft. Verify employers independently and provide sensitive payroll information only through a confirmed onboarding process.

Rehearse thirty days on the transition budget while employed and transfer the difference to reserves. Test autopay timing, search time, childcare, health needs and the realism of the household’s assumptions.

Prepare interviews and evaluate total compensation, benefits, start date and stability. Keep leads active until a written offer is verified. After reemployment, rebuild runway and maintain the career file.

Use confirmed warning signs proportionally while continuing to perform the current job. Public business information, official notices, reduced hours and eliminated projects are more useful than rumor, but none predicts an individual outcome with certainty.

Keep job-search activity on personal equipment and lawful personal time. Do not copy confidential records, customer lists, proprietary work or internal forecasts. Career preparation does not cancel employment duties or information-security rules.

If hours decline, update the transition budget and preserve pay records immediately. Ask the official state agency whether partial unemployment or another program may apply instead of assuming that only total job loss qualifies.

Put every deadline in one transition calendar: unemployment certifications, health enrollment, COBRA election, severance review, final pay, retirement-plan decisions and interviews. A missed deadline can cost more than a small spending cut saves.
Do not count verbal severance, an expected offer, unused credit or unvested stock as runway. Use settled cash and confirmed income for the base case, then show uncertain resources on a separate line.

The plan should preserve choice rather than demand perfect forecasting. A current résumé, benefit map, essential budget, cash reserve and secure search process are useful even when the recession or layoff never actually arrives unexpectedly.

faq.question: How much layoff runway is enough?
faq.answer: There is no universal amount. Base the target on essential burn, household incomes, job risk, health needs and realistic reemployment time.

faq.question: Should debt be paid off before building cash?
faq.answer: Keep minimums current and build a starter reserve, then balance guaranteed interest cost against the need for liquidity.

faq.question: When should unemployment be filed?
faq.answer: File promptly through the official state system after job loss if potentially eligible, and follow state certification rules.

faq.question: Does job loss qualify for Marketplace enrollment?
faq.answer: Loss of job-based coverage can create a Special Enrollment Period, subject to official timing and documentation rules.

faq.question: Should a 401(k) be rolled over immediately?
faq.answer: No. Compare leaving it, rolling to an eligible plan or IRA, and distribution consequences before acting.

faq.question: What job-search payment requests are suspicious?
faq.answer: Treat fees for a job, gift cards, cryptocurrency, check forwarding and required equipment purchases through a fake check as major warnings.

glossary.definition: The recurring amount needed for core household obligations during an income interruption.
Liquid resources expressed as time they can cover essential burn.
Federal continuation rights for certain employer group health plans after qualifying events.
A time-limited opportunity to enroll in coverage outside regular open enrollment after qualifying events.
Compensation or benefits provided at separation under an agreement, policy or applicable requirement.
The point at which specified employer retirement or equity benefits cannot be forfeited.
A reduced but livable spending plan activated by lower income or job loss.
A state-required unemployment claim step confirming ongoing eligibility facts for a week.
